subject: Follow-up: throughput & streaming qualification — QuantaCart pilot
messages:
From: Ethan Miles <ethan.miles@quantacart.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: QuantaCart Security <security@quantacart.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0500
Subject: QuantaCart pilot — throughput & streaming details

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. As promised, here’s a compact summary of our production characteristics so Redwood can help map requirements for the pilot: 

- Feature path: real-time cart scoring + autosuggest during checkout (streaming first-token and incremental tokens).
- Avg request size (tokens): 95 tokens (main payload) + ~20 tokens for system prompt = ~115 tokens typical.
- Request distribution: 70% short (40–80 tokens), 25% medium (80–200), 5% long (200–450).
- Steady-state: ~18 QPS (US east), average sustained concurrency ~12 active sessions.
- Peak burst: up to 220 QPS for ~60–120 seconds during flash sales; bursts occur ~2–3x/day.
- Per-request latency target: first-byte/streaming start <= 250ms (95th), completion acceptable up to 1.2s for long requests.
- Desired model behavior: streaming token-by-token for autosuggest; full-response generation for scoring.
- Multi-tenant: we will route 100% of checkout traffic to Redwood during pilot (no sensitive PII, but security team will want audit logs).

Attached a small sample of recent traces (quanta_workload_sample.csv) and a simplified architecture diagram. Please capture any unclear fields we should expand.

Next steps from our side: confirm timing for a short load-profile call and any synthetic-trace format you prefer.

Best,
Ethan
Ethan Miles
VP Product, QuantaCart
ethan.miles@quantacart.com
+1 415-555-0132

Attachments: quanta_workload_sample.csv, qcart_arch_diagram.png

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: QuantaCart pilot — throughput & streaming details

Thanks Ethan — great context and useful distribution. Quick recap + our asks so we can size the pilot: 

Recap of what we heard:
- Steady-state ~18 QPS, peaks to ~220 QPS for ~1–2 minutes, request token distribution skewed to short requests but with ~5% long tails.
- Streaming requirement for autosuggest (first-byte <= 250ms 95th) and full-generation for scoring.
- Audit/logging requirements from security.

Open clarifications we need from your infra/telemetry team: 
1) Are the flash-sale bursts correlated by region or global (do you see simultaneous spikes across multiple regions)?
2) Can you share a sample of concurrency over a 24h window (we can accept the CSV you attached but would like 1-min granularity if possible).
3) Any hard SLA/penalty definitions from your procurement team?

Proposed Redwood pilot sizing assumptions (we'll validate with internal perf tests):
- Baseline lanes: allocate capacity for 2x steady-state (36 QPS) and an autoscaling policy to cover up to 240 QPS burst with fallback to smaller/cheaper model variant if necessary.
- Latency SLOs: streaming-first-byte 95th <= 250ms; tail completion <= 1.5s for 99th on short requests.
- Concurrency: design for 400 concurrent inflight requests during bursts to account for long-tail tokens.
- Caching: recommend prefix cache for repeated prompts (we'll advise on TTL).

Immediate next steps: 
- Neha will propose an exact load-profile and synthetic trace format for your infra team to run a dry replay.
- Marissa will produce a pilot quote reflecting a Dedicated reserve vs hosted burst options and call out expected cost delta for 2-week stress run.
- Can we target a 30-minute load-profile sync next Wednesday (Nov 18)?

I attached a short sample plan as a starting point. If all good, we’ll schedule the sync and Neha will lead the test design.

— Avery
Avery Johnson
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Ethan Miles <ethan.miles@quantacart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Quota/profile — synthetic trace + sizing proposal

Thanks — I dug into the sample CSV and sketched a conservative mapping from tokens -> sustained throughput for a pilot. Key notes: 

- Mapping guidance: 1 QPS with avg 115 tokens ~= 115 tokens/sec; conversely 220 QPS at 115 tokens -> ~25k tokens/sec peak.
- For streaming, first-byte latency is dominated by model and network. To reliably hit 95th <= 250ms we recommend:
  * Prefer smaller/optimized model variants for autosuggest (quantized 7B or optimized 13B if your quality validation requires it).
  * Continuous batching disabled for autosuggest lanes (streaming) to avoid first-byte delays; enable batching on scoring lane to improve cost.
- Concurrency sizing: account for token generation parallelism — recommend capacity to handle 3x steady-state concurrency for short-term bursts (i.e., plan for ~36–45 concurrent model threads).

Suggested pilot plan (short):
1) Dry replay of 1 hour of real traces at 2x scale to validate autoscaling response and SLOs. We’ll provide a Dockerized replay harness.
2) Run targeted 5-min blast tests at 100%, 150%, 200% of observed peak to verify fallback policies.
3) Capture metrics: first-byte latency (stream), token/sec throughput, queue length, and model variant switch events.

Action item: Ethan — can you confirm 1-min granularity trace for the 24-hr window? If yes, I’ll prepare the replay harness and share run instructions by EOD tomorrow.

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Miles <ethan.miles@quantacart.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Pilot commercial/ops checklist

Looping in a couple of operational items from the pilot checklist: 

- Logging & audit: QuantaCart security asked for request/response hashes and token-level usage logs for the pilot. We can provide masked logs and audit stream; need to confirm retention period (default 30d).
- SLA framing: for pilot we’ll track SLOs but commercial SLA and credits are TBD until you move to Dedicated.
- Fallback policy: will outline a three-tier fallback (primary model -> smaller variant -> cached response) and instrument automatic circuit-breaker thresholds.
- Cost: I’ll attach a draft pilot quote (redwood-pilot-quote-draft.pdf) that shows Hosted baseline vs short Dedicated reserve to support 2-week stress runs.

Suggested timeline: run replay next week (Nov 18–20 window); we’ll reserve capacity for a 2-hour stress window during that period and share run times.

Questions for you, Ethan:
- Retention: does QuantaCart require >30 days for logs for compliance?
- Data export: any special S3/KMS rules for encryption at rest?

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

All — this looks good and aligned with our internal expectations. Quick answers: 
- Bursts are largely regional (US-east spike), not simultaneous global. That helps.
- We can produce the 1-min granularity 24h trace tomorrow morning and will add a short annotation for the two flash-sale windows.
- Retention: security asks for 90-day masked logs for the pilot — will that be supported?
- KMS: we require customer-managed keys for any S3 exports (we use AWS KMS).

We’re happy to run the replay on Nov 18 at 14:00 ET. Please send the replay harness and any pre-checklist.

Ethan
Ethan Miles
VP Product, QuantaCart
